Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, if the UE provided an APN for the establishment of the PDN connection, the UE shall stop timer T3396 if it is running for the APN provided by the UE. If the UE did not provide an APN for the establishment of the PDN connection and the request type was different from "emergency" and from "handover of emergency bearer services", the UE shall stop the timer T3396 associated with no APN if it is running. If the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message was received in response to a request for an emergency PDN connection, the UE shall not stop the timer T3396 associated with no APN if it is running. For any case, the UE shall then send an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message and enter the state BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE. When the default bearer is activated as part of the attach procedure, the UE shall send the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message together with ATTACH COMPLETE message. When the default bearer is activated as the response to the stand-alone PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, the UE shall send the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message alone
If a WLAN offload indication information element is included in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall store the WLAN offload acceptability values for this PDN connection and use the E-UTRAN offload acceptability value to determine whether this PDN connection is offloadable to WLAN or not
The UE checks the PTI in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message to identify the UE requested PDN connectivity procedure to which the default bearer context activation is related (see clause 6.5.1)
If the UE receives a serving PLMN rate control IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall store the serving PLMN rate control IE value and use the stored serving PLMN rate control value as the maximum allowed limit of uplink User data container IEs included in ESM DATA TRANSPORT messages for the corresponding PDN connection in accordance with 3GPP S 23.401 [10]
If the UE receives an APN rate control parameters container in the protocol configuration options IE or extended protocol configuration options IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall store the APN rate control parameters value and use the stored APN rate control parameters value as the maximum allowed limit of uplink user data related to the APN indicated in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message in accordance with 3GPP S 23.401 [10]. If the UE has a previously stored APN rate control parameters value for this APN, the UE shall replace the stored APN rate control parameters value for this APN with the received APN rate control parameters value
If the UE receives an additional APN rate control parameters for exception data container in the protocol configuration options IE or extended protocol configuration options IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall store the additional APN rate control parameters for exception data value and use the stored additional APN rate control parameters for exception data value as the maximum allowed limit of uplink exception data related to the APN indicated in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message in accordance with 3GPP S 23.401 [10]. If the UE has a previously stored additional APN rate control parameters for exception data value for this APN, the UE shall replace the stored additional APN rate control parameters for exception data value for this APN with the received additional APN rate control parameters for exception data value
If the UE receives a small data rate control parameters container in the protocol configuration options IE or the extended protocol configuration options IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall store the small data rate control parameters value and use the stored small data rate control parameters value as the maximum allowed limit of uplink user data for the corresponding PDU session that becomes transferred after inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode in accordance with 3GPP S 23.501 [58]
If the UE receives an additional small data rate control parameters for exception data container in the protocol configuration options IE or the extended protocol configuration options IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall store the additional small data rate control parameters for exception data value and use the stored additional small data rate control parameters for exception data value as the maximum allowed limit of uplink exception data for the corresponding PDU session that becomes transferred after inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode in accordance with 3GPP S 23.501 [58]
If the UE receives non-IP Link MTU parameter, Ethernet Frame Payload MTU parameter, IPv4 Link MTU parameter, or Unstructured Link MTU parameter of the protocol configuration options IE or of the extended protocol configuration options IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall pass the received Non-IP Link MTU size, Ethernet Frame Payload MTU size, or IPv4 Link MTU size, or Unstructured Link MTU size to the upper layer
NOTE 1: The Non-IP Link MTU and the IPv4 Link MTU size correspond to the maximum length of user data that can be sent either in the user data container in the ESM DATA TRANSPORT message or via S1-U interface
NOTE 2: The Ethernet frame payload MTU size corresponds to the maximum length of a payload of an Ethernet frame that can be sent either in the user data container in the ESM DATA TRANSPORT message or via S1-U interface
NOTE 3: A PDN connection of non-IP PDN type can be transferred to a PDU session of "Unstructured" PDU session type, thus the UE can request the unstructured link MTU parameter in the default EPS bearer context activation procedure. The unstructured link MTU size correspond to the maximum length of user data packet that can be sent either via the control plane or via N3 interface for a PDU session of the "Unstructured" PDU session type as specified in 3GPP S 24.501 [54]
If the UE receives the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message containing the Uplink data not allowed parameter in the extended protocol configuration options IE, then the UE shall not send any uplink user data over EPS bearer context(s) of the corresponding PDN connection
Upon receiving the DNS server security information, the UE shall pass it to the upper layer. The UE shall use this information to send the DNS over (D)TLS (See 3GPP S 33.501 [24])
NOTE 4: Support of DNS over (D)TLS is based on the informative requirements as specified in 3GPP S 33.501 [24]
If the UE supports provisioning of ECS configuration information to the EEC in the UE, then upon receiving
- at least one of ECS IPv4 address(es), ECS IPv6 address(es), ECS FQDN(s)
- at least one associated ECSP identifier; and
- optionally spatial validity conditions associated with the ECS address
in the Extended protocol configuration options IE of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall pass them to the upper layers
NOTE 5: The IP address(es) and/or FQDN(s) are associated with the ECSP identifier and replace previously provided ECS configuration information associated with the same ECSP identifier, if any.Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message, the MME shall enter the state BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE and stop the timer T3485, if the timer is running. If the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message included a low priority indicator set to "MS is configured for NAS signalling low priority", the MME shall store the NAS signalling low priority indication within the default EPS bearer context

results.question: What action must the UE take regarding the PDN connection if the SCEF or P-GW accepts the use of Reliable Data Service, and under which PDN connection conditions is the Reliable Data Service permitted?
results.reference: If the SCEF or P-GW accepts the use of Reliable Data Service, the UE shall use this PDN connection exclusively for data transfer using Reliable Data Service. The Reliable Data Service may only be used with PDN connections for which the 'Control plane only' indicator is set or with PDN connections using the control plane CIoT EPS optimization when the MME does not move such PDN connections to the user plane.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.11, Handling of Reliable Data Service; TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.11, Handling of Reliable Data Service
results.model_answer:
**UE action:** If the SCEF or P-GW accepts the UE's request for Reliable Data Service usage (indicated via extended PCO IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message), the UE **shall use that PDN connection exclusively for data transfer using Reliable Data Service**. Otherwise, the UE shall not use that PDN connection for Reliable Data Service.

**Permitted conditions:** Reliable Data Service may only be used with PDN connections that:
- have the **"Control plane only" indicator set**, or
- use **control plane CIoT EPS optimization**, provided the MME does **not** move that PDN connection to the user plane.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.11, Handling of Reliable Data Service

General
Entities:
- Paging procedure using S-TMSI (Procedure): Network-initiated paging procedure for EPS services using S-TMSI with CN domain indicator set to PS. Used when NAS signalling messages, cdma2000 signalling messages, or user data is pending to be sent to the UE and no NAS signalling connection exists.
- Paging message (Message): Message sent by the network to page the UE. May include Voice Service Indication when voice service data is pending.
- Voice Service Indication (Information Element): Optional indication included in Paging message when pending user data is related to voice service and network supports paging indication for voice services.
- Extended DRX parameters (Information Element): IE provided to UE during attach or tracking area updating procedure that contains eDRX configuration.
- Timer T3413 (Timer): Timer started by network for paging procedure when eDRX is not used or UE has PDN connection for emergency bearer services. Network may reinitiate paging upon expiry.
- Timer T3415 (Timer): Timer started by network for paging procedure when network accepted to use eDRX for UE and UE does not have PDN connection for emergency bearer services. Must be set smaller than T3-RESPONSE.
- EMM-IDLE mode (State): UE state where no NAS signalling connection exists. UE may be in EMM-IDLE with or without suspend indication.
- Paging restriction conditions (Condition): Conditions based on stored paging restriction type that determine whether network should initiate paging procedure. Includes restrictions for all paging, voice service exceptions, and PDN connection exceptions.
- eDRX active condition (Condition): Condition where network has accepted to use eDRX for UE and UE does not have PDN connection for emergency bearer services.
- Paging with priority (Property): Network behavior to initiate paging with priority when receiving downlink signalling or data associated with priority EPS bearers while waiting for response to non-priority paging.

- Paging procedure using S-TMSI --starts--> Timer T3413: Paging procedure starts timer T3413 when eDRX is not used or UE has emergency PDN connection
- Paging procedure using S-TMSI --starts--> Timer T3415: Paging procedure starts timer T3415 when eDRX is active and no emergency PDN connection exists

- Extended DRX parameters --guards_by--> eDRX active condition: eDRX active condition is determined by Extended DRX parameters IE provided to UE
- Paging restriction conditions --establishes--> Paging with priority: Paging restriction conditions establish when paging with priority should be initiated

retrieved_contexts.text:
Linkage between the protocols for EPS mobility management and EPS session management
Entities:
- EPS Attach Procedure (Procedure): Procedure for UE registration with the network, which can include default EPS bearer context activation.
- Default EPS Bearer Context Activation Procedure (Procedure): Procedure to establish a default EPS bearer context, potentially transmitted within EPS mobility management messages during attach.
- Dedicated EPS Bearer Context Activation Procedure (Procedure): Procedure to establish one or several dedicated EPS bearer contexts for PDN connections of IP or Ethernet type.
- Service Request Procedure (Procedure): Procedure initiated by UE for transport of user data via control plane, especially in EMM-IDLE mode.
- CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST Message (Message): Message used in service request procedure for control plane CIoT EPS optimization, which can contain ESM DATA TRANSPORT message.
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT Message (Message): ESM message transmitted within CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message for user data transport via control plane.
- EMM-REGISTERED (State): EPS Mobility Management state indicating UE is registered with the network.
- EMM-IDLE (State): EPS Mobility Management state where UE is not actively communicating but registered.
- EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection (Condition): Condition where UE is registered but has no PDN connection, which may not be supported by UE or MME.
- Suspend ESM message transmission (Property): Behavior where UE or MME suspends transmission of ESM messages during certain EMM procedures.
Relations:
- EPS Attach Procedure --has_step--> Default EPS Bearer Context Activation Procedure: Default EPS bearer context activation can be performed as part of the attach procedure.
- EPS Attach Procedure --has_step--> Dedicated EPS Bearer Context Activation Procedure: Dedicated EPS bearer context activation can be performed in parallel during attach procedure.
- EPS Attach Procedure --requires_state--> Default EPS Bearer Context Activation Procedure: Attach procedure completion is dependent on default EPS bearer activation if EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is not supported.
- EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection --guards_by--> EPS Attach Procedure: Condition that attach success depends on default bearer activation if EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is not supported.
- CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST Message --contains_IE--> ESM DATA TRANSPORT Message: CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message contains ESM DATA TRANSPORT message as an information element.
- Service Request Procedure --has_step--> CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST Message: Service request procedure involves transmission of CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message.
- Service Request Procedure --requires_state--> EMM-IDLE: Service request procedure can be initiated by UE in EMM-IDLE mode for control plane data transport.
- Suspend ESM message transmission --guards_by--> EPS Attach Procedure: ESM message transmission is not suspended during attach procedure.
- Suspend ESM message transmission --guards_by--> Service Request Procedure: ESM message transmission is not suspended during service request procedure for control plane data transport.

If the UE supports Reliable Data Service (see 3GPP S 24.250 [51]), the UE may request data transfer using Reliable Data Service for a PDN connection in the extended protocol configuration options IE during attach and UE-requested PDN connectivity procedures (see clause 5.5.1 and 6.5.1)
The Reliable Data Service may only be used with PDN connections for which the "Control plane only" indicator is set or with PDN connections using the control plane CIoT EPS optimization when the MME does not move such PDN connections to the user plane
The SCEF or P-GW shall inform the UE about the acceptance of UE 's request for Reliable Data Service usage during the activation of the default bearer of a PDN connection (see clause 6.4.1) in the extended protocol configuration options IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message
If the SCEF or P-GW accepts the use of Reliable Data Service to transfer data for the specified PDN connection, the UE shall use this PDN connection exclusively for data transfer using Reliable Data Service; otherwise the UE shall not use this PDN connection for data transfer using Reliable Data Service

Upon receipt of the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, the MME checks whether the ESM information transfer flag is included. If the flag is included the MME waits for completion of the ESM information request procedure before proceeding with the PDN connectivity procedure. The MME then checks if connectivity with the requested PDN can be established. If no requested APN is included in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message or the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message and the request type is different from "emergency" and from "handover of emergency bearer services" and from "RLOS", the MME shall use the default APN as the requested APN. If the request type is "emergency" or "handover of emergency bearer services", the MME shall use the APN configured for emergency bearer services or select the statically configured PDN GW for unauthenticated UEs, if applicable. If the request type is "RLOS", the MME shall use the APN configured for RLOS
If the network receives a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message with the same combination of APN and PDN type as an already existing PDN connection, and multiple PDN connections for a given APN are allowed, the network retains the existing EPS bearer contexts for the PDN connection and proceeds with the requested PDN connectivity procedure
If the lower layers provide a GW Transport Layer Address value identifying a L-GW together with the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message and a PDN connection is established as a LIPA PDN connection due to the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, then the MME shall store the GW Transport Layer Address value as the P-GW address in the EPS bearer context of the LIPA PDN connection
If the lower layers provide a SIPTO L-GW Transport Layer Address value identifying a L-GW together with the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message and a PDN connection is established as a SIPTO at the local network PDN connection due to the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, then the MME shall store the SIPTO L-GW Transport Layer Address value as the P-GW address in the EPS bearer context of the SIPTO at the local network PDN connection
If the lower layers provide a LHN-ID value together with the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message and a PDN connection is established as a SIPTO at the local network PDN connection due to the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, then the MME shall store the LHN-ID value in the EPS bearer context of the SIPTO at the local network PDN connection
NOTE 1: The receipt of a LHN-ID value during the establishment of the PDN connection, during tracking area updating procedure or during inter-MME handover can be used as an indication by the MME that the SIPTO at the local network PDN connection is established to a stand-alone GW (see 3GPP S 23.401 [10])
If connectivity with the requested PDN is accepted by the network, the MME shall initiate the default EPS bearer context activation procedure (see clause 6.4.1)
If connectivity with the requested PDN is accepted and the network considers this PDN connection a LIPA PDN connection, then subject to operator policy the MME shall include in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message the Connectivity type IE indicating "the PDN connection is considered a LIPA PDN connection"
If connectivity with the requested PDN is accepted, but with a restriction of IP version (i.e. both an IPv4 address and an IPv6 prefix is requested, but only one particular IP version, or only single IP version bearers are supported/allowed by the network), ESM cause #50 "PDN type IPv4 only allowed", #51 "PDN type IPv6 only allowed", or #52 "single address bearers only allowed", respectively, shall be included in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message
If connectivity with the requested PDN is accepted and the UE provided the Header compression configuration IE in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, the MME may include the Header compression configuration IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message. Furthermore, if the MME decides that the associated PDN connection is only for control plane CIoT EPS optimization (see clause 5.3.15), the MME shall include the Control plane only indication in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message
Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, the UE shall stop timer T3482 and enter the state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE. The UE should ensure that the procedure transaction identity (PTI) assigned to this procedure is not released immediately. The way to achieve this is implementation dependent. While the PTI value is not released, the UE regards any received ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message with the same PTI value as a network retransmission (see clause 7.3.1)
Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message with the Connectivity type IE indicating "the PDN connection is considered a LIPA PDN connection", the UE provides an indication to the upper layers that the connectivity is provided by a LIPA PDN connection
Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, if the 3GPP PS data off UE status is "activated", the UE behaves as described in clause 6.3.10
Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, if the SCEF or P-GW indicates acceptance of use of Reliable Data Service to transfer data for the PDN connection, the UE behaves as described in clause 6.3.11
Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, if an S-NSSAI and the PLMN ID that this S-NSSAI relates to are provided in the protocol configuration options IE or extended protocol configuration options IE, the UE shall delete the stored S-NSSAI and the PLMN ID that this S-NSSAI relates to, if any, and shall store the S-NSSAI and the PLMN ID this S-NSSAI relates to provided in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message and the associated PLMN ID along with the corresponding PDU session ID that the UE provided in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message. The usage of the PDU session ID and the corresponding S-NSSAI with the associated PLMN ID is specified in 3GPP S 24.501 [54]. Additionally, the UE shall remove the S-NSSAI, if present, from the rejected NSSAI as specified in 3GPP S 24.501 [54] clause 4.6.2.2
Upon receipt of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message with a session-AMBR and QoS rule(s), which correspond to the default EPS bearer of the PDN connectivity being activated, in the protocol configuration options IE or the extended protocol configuration options IE, the UE stores the session-AMBR and QoS rule(s) for use during inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode
If the UE requests the PDN type "IPv4v6", receives the selected PDN type set to "IPv4" and the ESM cause value #50 "PDN type IPv4 only allowed", the UE shall not automatically send another PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message to the same APN (or no APN, if no APN was indicated by the UE) to obtain a PDN type different from the one allowed by the network until
- the UE is registered to a new PLMN
- the UE is switched off; or
- the USIM is removed
If the UE requests the PDN type "IPv4v6", receives the selected PDN type set to "IPv6" and the ESM cause value #51 "PDN type IPv6 only allowed", the UE shall not automatically send another PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message to the same APN (or no APN, if no APN was indicated by the UE) to obtain a PDN type different from the one allowed by the network until
- the UE is registered to a new PLMN
- the UE is switched off; or
- the USIM is removed
NOTE 2: For the ESM cause values #50 "PDN type IPv4 only allowed" and #51 "PDN type IPv6 only allowed", re-attempt in A/Gb, Iu, or N1 mode for the same APN (or no APN, if no APN was indicated by the UE) is only allowed using the PDN type(s) indicated by the network

results.justification: The model answer correctly captures both core requirements: (1) the UE shall use the PDN connection exclusively for data transfer using Reliable Data Service when accepted, and (2) the permitted conditions are PDN connections with the 'Control plane only' indicator set, or PDN connections using control plane CIoT EPS optimization when the MME does not move them to the user plane. This fully aligns with the reference answer with no contradictions.

results.question: According to the principles of address handling, what value should the EPS bearer identity be set to when the UE initiates a transaction related procedure, and what is the corresponding state of the procedure transaction in the UE at that moment?
results.reference: When the UE initiates a transaction related procedure, it shall set the EPS bearer identity to 'no EPS bearer identity assigned'. At that moment, the procedure transaction state in the UE is 'PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING', meaning the UE has initiated a procedure transaction towards the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.2, Principles of address handling for ESM procedures; TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.2.4, PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING
results.model_answer:
When the UE initiates a transaction related procedure, it shall set the EPS bearer identity to **"no EPS bearer identity assigned"** in the ESM message header (while including a valid Procedure Transaction Identity value).

Regarding the corresponding state, the context indicates that after sending the initial transaction related request message, the UE enters the **PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING** state (as reflected, e.g., in clause 6.6.1.2.2 for ESM information request/response exchanges and clause 6.6.3.2 for REMOTE UE REPORT), remaining in this state until the response is received, at which point it transitions to PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.2, Principles of address handling for ESM procedures

retrieved_contexts.clause_title: Principles of address handling for ESM procedures
retrieved_contexts.text:
Principles of address handling for ESM procedures
Entities:
- Transaction related procedure (Procedure): ESM procedures that use the procedure transaction identity as address parameter in the ESM message header. When initiated, entities include a valid PTI value and set EBI to 'no EPS bearer identity assigned'.
- EPS bearer context related procedure (Procedure): ESM procedures that use the EPS bearer identity as address parameter in the ESM message header. When network-initiated, includes valid EBI value with PTI set based on trigger condition.
- Procedure transaction identity (Identifier): Address parameter used in transaction related procedures. Can be set to valid value or 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'.
- EPS bearer identity (Identifier): Address parameter used in EPS bearer context related procedures. Can be set to valid value or 'no EPS bearer identity assigned'.
- Transaction related request message (Message): Initial message in transaction related procedures containing PTI and EBI parameters.
- Transaction related response message (Message): Response message in transaction related procedures containing PTI and EBI parameters.
- EPS bearer context related request (Message): Request message in EPS bearer context related procedures containing EBI and PTI parameters.
- EPS bearer context related response (Message): Response message in EPS bearer context related procedures containing EBI and PTI parameters.
- Triggered by transaction related request (Condition): Condition where EPS bearer context procedure is triggered by receipt of transaction related request message from UE.
- Network-internal trigger (Condition): Condition where EPS bearer context procedure is triggered network-internally.
- Triggered by user data transport via control plane (Condition): Condition where EPS bearer context procedure is triggered by transport of user data via control plane.
Relations:
- Transaction related procedure --contains_IE--> Procedure transaction identity: Transaction related procedures use PTI as address parameter in ESM message header.
- Transaction related procedure --contains_IE--> EPS bearer identity: Transaction related procedures set EBI to 'no EPS bearer identity assigned'.
- EPS bearer context related procedure --contains_IE--> EPS bearer identity: EPS bearer context related procedures use EBI as address parameter in ESM message header.
- EPS bearer context related procedure --contains_IE--> Procedure transaction identity: EPS bearer context related procedures include PTI parameter with value based on trigger condition.
- Transaction related request message --contains_IE--> Procedure transaction identity: Transaction related request messages contain PTI parameter.
- Transaction related request message --contains_IE--> EPS bearer identity: Transaction related request messages contain EBI parameter.
- EPS bearer context related request --contains_IE--> EPS bearer identity: EPS bearer context related request messages contain EBI parameter.
- EPS bearer context related request --contains_IE--> Procedure transaction identity: EPS bearer context related request messages contain PTI parameter.
- Triggered by transaction related request --guards_by--> Procedure transaction identity: When triggered by transaction related request, PTI value from request is included in EPS bearer context request.
- Network-internal trigger --guards_by--> Procedure transaction identity: When triggered network-internally, PTI is set to 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'.
- Triggered by user data transport via control plane --guards_by--> Procedure transaction identity: When triggered by user data transport via control plane, PTI is set to 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'.
- EPS bearer context related response --contains_IE--> EPS bearer identity: EPS bearer context related response messages contain EBI value received from network.
- EPS bearer context related response --contains_IE--> Procedure transaction identity: EPS bearer context related response messages set PTI to 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'.

Remote UE Report initiated by the UE
Entities:
- Remote UE Report procedure (Procedure): Procedure initiated by the UE to report information about newly connected or disconnected remote UEs to the network.
- REMOTE UE REPORT (Message): Message sent by the UE to the network to initiate the Remote UE Report procedure.
- REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE (Message): Message sent by the network to the UE in response to the REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- Remote UE information (Information Element): Information about newly connected or disconnected remote UEs included in the REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- Encrypted IMSI remote UE identity (Information Element): Encrypted IMSI identity of a remote UE included in the REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- ProSe Key Management Function address (Information Element): Address of the ProSe Key Management Function corresponding to an encrypted IMSI remote UE identity.
- Default EPS bearer identity (Information Element): Identity of the default EPS bearer associated with the PDN connection for the remote UE.
- T3493 (Timer): Timer started by the UE when sending the REMOTE UE REPORT message and stopped upon receipt of the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message.
- PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING (State): State entered by the UE after sending the REMOTE UE REPORT message and starting timer T3493.
- PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE (State): State entered by the UE after receiving the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message and stopping timer T3493.
- Encrypted IMSI present (Condition): Condition that if any encrypted IMSI remote UE identity is included in the REMOTE UE REPORT message, the UE shall include the corresponding ProSe Key Management Function address.

- REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE --requires_state--> PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE: After receiving the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message, the UE enters the PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE state.

Reception of an ESM STATUS message by an ESM entity
Entities:
- ESM STATUS message (Message): Message sent to report certain error conditions detected upon receipt of ESM protocol data. Can be sent by both MME and UE.
- ESM cause #43 (Invalid EPS bearer identity) (Condition): Error condition indicating an invalid EPS bearer identity was received.
- ESM cause #81 (Invalid PTI value) (Condition): Error condition indicating an invalid Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) value was received.
- ESM cause #97 (Message type non-existent or not implemented) (Condition): Error condition indicating a message type that is non-existent or not implemented was received.
- Abort ongoing ESM procedure (Procedure): Procedure to abort any ongoing ESM procedure related to the received EPS bearer identity or PTI value.
- Stop related timer (Procedure): Action to stop any timer related to the aborted ESM procedure.
- Deactivate EPS bearer context locally (Procedure): Procedure to deactivate the corresponding EPS bearer context locally without peer-to-peer signaling.
- EPS bearer identity (Identifier): Identifier for an EPS bearer context.
- Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) (Identifier): Identifier for an ESM procedure transaction.
Relations:
- ESM STATUS message --guards_by--> ESM cause #43 (Invalid EPS bearer identity): ESM STATUS message behavior is determined by ESM cause value #43.
- ESM STATUS message --guards_by--> ESM cause #81 (Invalid PTI value): ESM STATUS message behavior is determined by ESM cause value #81.

- Abort ongoing ESM procedure --guards_by--> EPS bearer identity: Abort procedure may be related to EPS bearer identity.

- PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING (State): State entered by network after sending ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message.

Transaction related procedures use the procedure transaction identity as address parameter in the ESM message header. When the UE or the network initiates a transaction related procedure, it shall include a valid procedure transaction identity value in the message header and set the EPS bearer identity to "no EPS bearer identity assigned". When the ProSe UE-to-network relay initiates the transaction related procedure remote UE report, it shall include a valid procedure transaction identity value in the message header and set the EPS bearer identity to a valid EPS bearer identity value
If the response message is again a transaction related message, e.g. a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT, PDN DISCONNECT REJECT, BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT, BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REJECT, ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message or ESM DUMMY MESSAGE from the network or an ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message or ESM DUMMY MESSAGE from the UE, the sending entity shall include the procedure transaction identity value received with the request message and set the EPS bearer identity to "no EPS bearer identity assigned" (see examples in figures 6.3.2.1, 6.3.2.1a and 6.3.2.2). If the response message is the transaction related message REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message from the network, the network shall include the procedure transaction identity value received with the request message and set the EPS bearer identity to the EPS bearer identity value received from the ProSe UE-to-network relay (see example in figure 6.3.2.2a)
If an ESM DUMMY MESSAGE is sent in response to a received ESM DUMMY MESSAGE, the sending entity shall include the received procedure transaction identity value in the message header and set the EPS bearer identity to "no EPS bearer identity assigned"
Figure 6.3.2.1: Transaction related procedure initiated by the UE and rejected by the network
Figure 6.3.2.1a: Transaction related procedure initiated by the UE and responded by a network initiated transaction related request
Figure 6.3.2.2: Transaction related procedure initiated by the network
Figure 6.3.2.2a: Transaction related procedure initiated by the UE
EPS bearer context related procedures use the EPS bearer identity as address parameter in the ESM message header. When the network initiates an EPS bearer context related procedure, it shall include a valid EPS bearer identity value in the message header. The procedure transaction identity value shall be set as follows
- If the EPS bearer context related procedure was triggered by the receipt of a transaction related request message from the UE, the network shall include the procedure transaction identity value received with the transaction related request message in the message header of the EPS bearer context related request message (see example in figure 6.3.2.3)
- If the procedure was triggered network-internally, the network shall set the procedure transaction identity value in the message header of the EPS bearer context related request message to "no procedure transaction identity assigned" (see example in figure 6.3.2.4)
- If the procedure was triggered by the transport of user data via the control plane, the network shall set the procedure transaction identity value in the message header of the EPS bearer context related request message to "no procedure transaction identity assigned" (see example in figure 6.3.2.5)
In the response message of the EPS bearer context related procedure, the UE shall include the EPS bearer identity value received from the network and set the procedure transaction identity value to "no procedure transaction identity assigned"
When the UE initiates an EPS bearer context related procedure and the procedure was triggered by the transport of user data via the control plane, it shall include a valid EPS bearer identity value and set the procedure transaction identity value to "no procedure transaction identity assigned" in the message header (see example in figure 6.3.2.6)
Figure 6.3.2.3: EPS bearer context related procedure triggered by a transaction related request
Figure 6.3.2.4: EPS bearer context related procedure triggered network-internally
Figure 6.3.2.5: EPS bearer context related procedure triggered by network for the transport of user data via the control plane
Figure 6.3.2.6: EPS bearer context related procedure triggered by UE for the transport of user data via the control plane

Upon receipt of the BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message, the MME checks whether the resources requested by the UE can be established, modified or released by verifying the EPS bearer identity given in the EPS bearer identity for packet filter IE
If the bearer resource modification requested is accepted by the network, the MME shall initiate either a dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure, an EPS bearer context modification procedure or an EPS bearer context deactivation procedure
If the request to re-negotiate header compression configuration associated to an EPS bearer context is accepted by the network, the MME shall initiate an EPS bearer context modification procedure
If the bearer resource modification requests a release of bearer resources that results in the TFT of the EPS bearer context containing only packet filters applicable to the uplink direction, the network may initiate the EPS bearer context deactivation procedure
Upon receipt of an ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST or DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message with a PTI which matches the value used for the BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message, the UE shall stop timer T3481 and enter the state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE. The UE should ensure that the procedure transaction identity (PTI) assigned to this procedure is not released immediately. The way to achieve this is implementation dependent. While the PTI value is not released, the UE regards any received ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST or MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST or DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message with the same PTI value as a network retransmission (see clause 7.3.1)
i) If the ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message is received, the UE shall verify that the EPS bearer identity given in the EPS bearer identity IE is not already used by any EPS bearer context. The UE shall then proceed as described in clause 6.4.2.3 or clause 6.4.2.4
ii) If the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message is received, the UE verifies that the EPS bearer identity given in the EPS bearer identity IE is any of the active EPS bearer contexts. The UE shall then proceed as described in clause 6.4.3.3 or clause 6.4.3.4
iii) If the DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message is received, the UE verifies that the EPS bearer identity given in the EPS bearer identity IE is one of the active EPS bearer contexts. The UE shall then proceed as described in clause 6.4.4.3
In case i, after successful completion of the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure, the network may initiate an EPS bearer context modification procedure to delete the packet filters which have packet filter identifiers indicated by the UE in the Traffic flow aggregate IE in the BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message and for which the network created new packet filters during the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure. In this case the MME shall set the procedure transaction identity value in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message to "no procedure transaction identity assigned"

The eCall inactivity procedure is applicable only to a UE configured for eCall only mode as specified in 3GPP S 31.102 [17]. The procedure shall be started when
- the UE is in any EMM-REGISTERED substate except substates EMM-REGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH or EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE
- the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode; and
- one of the following conditions applies
1) timer T3444 expires or is found to have already expired and timer T3445 is not running
2) timer T3445 expires or is found to have already expired and timer T3444 is not running; or
3) timers T3444 and T3445 expire or are found to have already expired
The UE shall then perform the following actions
- stop other running timers (e.g. T3411, T3412)
- if the UE is currently registered to EPS services only, perform a detach procedure for EPS services only
- if the UE is currently registered for both EPS services and non-EPS services, perform a combined detach procedure for EPS services and non-EPS services
- delete any GUTI, TAI list, last visited registered TAI, list of equivalent PLMNs, and eKSI; and
- enter EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE state

results.question: Where is the procedure transaction identity located in an ESM message header, and what is the network's procedure transaction state when it has initiated a transaction towards the UE?
results.reference: The procedure transaction identity is located in bits 1 to 8 of the second octet (octet 1a) of every EPS Session Management (ESM) message. When the network has initiated a procedure transaction towards the UE, its state is 'PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.4, Procedure transaction identity; TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.3.7, PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING
results.model_answer:
Per TS 24.301, the Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) is carried as an address parameter in the **ESM message header** itself (used for transaction related procedures, as opposed to the EPS bearer identity used for EPS bearer context related procedures).

Regarding the network's state: when the network has initiated a procedure transaction towards the UE (e.g., by sending a transaction related request message such as ESM INFORMATION REQUEST) and is awaiting the UE's response, the network is in the **PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING** state (clause 6.1.3.3.7). It returns to **PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE** once the UE sends its ESM procedure response.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.3.7, PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING

retrieved_contexts.text:
ESM information request initiated by the network
Entities:
- ESM information request procedure (Procedure): Network-initiated procedure to request ESM information from the UE. The network sends ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message, starts timer T3489, and enters PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING state.

- ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE (Message): Message sent by UE to network in response to ESM INFORMATION REQUEST. Contains protocol configuration options, APN if required, and PTI from request message.
- T3489 (Timer): Timer started by network when sending ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message and stopped upon receipt of ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE.
- PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING (State): State entered by network after sending ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message.
- PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE (State): State entered by network after receiving ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message.
- Security context setup (Condition): Condition requiring that security context has been established before ESM INFORMATION REQUEST can be sent.
- ESM information transfer flag set (Condition): Condition requiring that ESM information transfer flag has been set in PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message.
- Procedure Transaction Identity (Information Element): Procedure Transaction Identity included in ESM INFORMATION REQUEST and ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE messages.
- EPS bearer identity (Information Element): EPS bearer identity set to 'no EPS bearer identity assigned' in both ESM INFORMATION REQUEST and ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE messages.

Transaction related procedures use the procedure transaction identity as address parameter in the ESM message header. When the UE or the network initiates a transaction related procedure, it shall include a valid procedure transaction identity value in the message header and set the EPS bearer identity to "no EPS bearer identity assigned". When the ProSe UE-to-network relay initiates the transaction related procedure remote UE report, it shall include a valid procedure transaction identity value in the message header and set the EPS bearer identity to a valid EPS bearer identity value
If the response message is again a transaction related message, e.g. a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT, PDN DISCONNECT REJECT, BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT, BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REJECT, ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message or ESM DUMMY MESSAGE from the network or an ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message or ESM DUMMY MESSAGE from the UE, the sending entity shall include the procedure transaction identity value received with the request message and set the EPS bearer identity to "no EPS bearer identity assigned" (see examples in figures 6.3.2.1, 6.3.2.1a and 6.3.2.2). If the response message is the transaction related message REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message from the network, the network shall include the procedure transaction identity value received with the request message and set the EPS bearer identity to the EPS bearer identity value received from the ProSe UE-to-network relay (see example in figure 6.3.2.2a)
If an ESM DUMMY MESSAGE is sent in response to a received ESM DUMMY MESSAGE, the sending entity shall include the received procedure transaction identity value in the message header and set the EPS bearer identity to "no EPS bearer identity assigned"

Figure 6.3.2.1a: Transaction related procedure initiated by the UE and responded by a network initiated transaction related request
Figure 6.3.2.2: Transaction related procedure initiated by the network
Figure 6.3.2.2a: Transaction related procedure initiated by the UE
EPS bearer context related procedures use the EPS bearer identity as address parameter in the ESM message header. When the network initiates an EPS bearer context related procedure, it shall include a valid EPS bearer identity value in the message header. The procedure transaction identity value shall be set as follows
- If the EPS bearer context related procedure was triggered by the receipt of a transaction related request message from the UE, the network shall include the procedure transaction identity value received with the transaction related request message in the message header of the EPS bearer context related request message (see example in figure 6.3.2.3)
- If the procedure was triggered network-internally, the network shall set the procedure transaction identity value in the message header of the EPS bearer context related request message to "no procedure transaction identity assigned" (see example in figure 6.3.2.4)
- If the procedure was triggered by the transport of user data via the control plane, the network shall set the procedure transaction identity value in the message header of the EPS bearer context related request message to "no procedure transaction identity assigned" (see example in figure 6.3.2.5)
In the response message of the EPS bearer context related procedure, the UE shall include the EPS bearer identity value received from the network and set the procedure transaction identity value to "no procedure transaction identity assigned"
When the UE initiates an EPS bearer context related procedure and the procedure was triggered by the transport of user data via the control plane, it shall include a valid EPS bearer identity value and set the procedure transaction identity value to "no procedure transaction identity assigned" in the message header (see example in figure 6.3.2.6)

results.question: For a UE operating in WB-S1 mode via satellite E-UTRAN access, what determines the applicable NAS timer values for the UE and the MME, and is the restriction on use of enhanced coverage considered in this determination?
results.reference: For a UE in WB-S1 mode via satellite E-UTRAN access, Clause 4.8.2 specifies that the UE shall apply the value of the applicable NAS timer indicated in tables 10.2.1 and 10.3.1 for WB-S1/CE mode. The supporting MME shall calculate the value of the applicable NAS timer indicated in tables 10.2.2 and 10.3.2 for WB-S1/CE mode. The NOTE in Clause 4.8.2 explicitly states that when using satellite E-UTRAN access, the restriction on use of enhanced coverage indication from the network is NOT considered when determining the applicable NAS timers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.2, UE using satellite E-UTRAN access; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.16, Restriction on use of enhanced coverage
results.model_answer:
For a UE operating in WB-S1 mode via satellite E-UTRAN access:

- **UE side:** The UE shall apply the applicable NAS timer values indicated in Table 10.2.1 and Table 10.3.1 for WB-S1/CE mode. The value is calculated at the start of the NAS procedure and is not re-calculated until the procedure is completed, restarted, or aborted.

- **MME side:** An MME that supports WB-S1 mode and performs NAS signalling with the UE via satellite E-UTRAN access shall calculate the applicable NAS timer values indicated in Table 10.2.2 and Table 10.3.2 for WB-S1/CE mode, following the same start-of-procedure calculation rule.

- **Enhanced coverage restriction:** No, it is **not** considered. Per the NOTE in clause 4.8.2, when using satellite E-UTRAN access, the restriction on use of enhanced coverage indication from the network is disregarded when determining the applicable NAS timers—unlike the non-satellite case (clause 4.8.1), where such restriction (or CE mode B restriction) is a precondition for using the WB-S1/CE mode timer values.

results.question: When a UE is in NB-S1 mode via satellite E-UTRAN access, which clause specifies the calculation of the applicable NAS timer values for the UE and the MME, and what is the key characteristic of this calculation?
results.reference: Clause 4.7 specifies that for a UE in NB-S1 mode, the UE shall calculate the applicable NAS timer values indicated in table 10.2.1 plus 240s and table 10.3.1 plus 180s. The MME shall calculate the values indicated in table 10.2.2 plus 240s and table 10.3.2 plus 180s. A key characteristic is that the NAS timer value shall be calculated at the start of a NAS procedure and shall not be re-calculated until the procedure is completed, restarted, or aborted. Furthermore, NOTE 2 in Clause 4.7 states that as NB-S1 mode includes satellite access, these timer values also apply for satellite access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.7, EPS mobility management and EPS session management in NB-S1 mode; TS 24.301, Clause 4.11.1, General
results.model_answer:
Clause 4.7 (EPS mobility management and EPS session management in NB-S1 mode) specifies this, since NOTE 2 states that NB-S1 mode includes the case of satellite access, so the timer values in this clause apply also for satellite E-UTRAN access.

**Key characteristic of the calculation:**
- The UE calculates the applicable NAS timer as the base value from **Table 10.2.1 plus a 240s offset**, and the value from **Table 10.3.1 plus a 180s offset**.
- The MME (supporting NB-S1 mode) calculates the applicable NAS timer as the base value from **Table 10.2.2 plus a 240s offset**, and the value from **Table 10.3.2 plus a 180s offset**.
- In both cases, the timer value is **calculated once at the start of the NAS procedure** and is **not re-calculated** until the procedure is completed, restarted, or aborted.

results.question: A UE configured for eCall only mode is powered on with a valid USIM present. According to the rules for selecting the substate after power on, what substate should it initially enter, and under what condition would it later transition to EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE?
results.reference: After power on, the UE should initially enter the PLMN-SEARCH substate. It would later transition to EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE when timers T3444 and T3445 have expired or are not running, a PLMN has been selected, and the UE does not need to perform an eCall over IMS or a call to a non-emergency MSISDN/URI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.3.9, EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE
results.model_answer:
The UE initially enters **PLMN-SEARCH**, since the USIM is available and valid at power on (timers T3444 and T3445 are also considered expired at power on for eCall-only mode).

It later transitions to **EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE** once, following PLMN-SEARCH, the UE is configured for eCall only mode (as specified in 3GPP TS 31.102) — this condition alone determines the substate selection to eCALL-INACTIVE after power on.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on

Entities:
- PLMN-SEARCH (State): Initial substate entered when UE is powered on with valid USIM available.

- NO-IMSI (State): Substate entered when no USIM is present in the UE.

For a UE configured for eCall only mode as specified in 3GPP S 31.102 [17], timers T3444 and T3445 are considered to have expired at power on. When the UE is switched on, the substate shall be PLMN-SEARCH if the USIM is available and valid. See 3GPP S 23.122 [6] for further details
The substate chosen after PLMN-SEARCH, following power on is
- if no cell can be selected, the substate shall be NO-CELL-AVAILABLE
- if no USIM is present, the substate shall be NO-IMSI
- if a suitable cell has been found and the PLMN or tracking area is not in the forbidden list, then the substate shall be NORMAL-SERVICE
- if the selected cell is known not to be able to provide normal service, then the UE shall enter the substate LIMITED-SERVICE
- if the UE is in manual network selection mode and no cell of the selected PLMN has been found, the UE shall enter the substate NO-CELL-AVAILABLE
- if the selected cell is a non-3GPP cell, the substate shall be NO-CELL-AVAILABLE; and
- if the UE is configured for eCall only mode as specified in 3GPP S 31.102 [17], the substate shall be eCALL-INACTIVE

retrieved_contexts.text: The UE shall perform cell selection according to 3GPP S 36.304 [21] and choose an appropriate substate when a cell is found. When the lower layers indicate to prepare for an S101 mode to S1 mode handover and the PLMN identity of the target cell provided with this indication is not in one of forbidden PLMN lists, the UE shall enter substate NORMAL-SERVICE NOTE: It is assumed that the UE can determine the PLMN identity of networks supporting cdma2000 xae HRPD access from the information broadcast over the radio interface. For the purpose of S101 mode to S1 mode handover, the UE can use the PLMN identity of the visited cdma2000 xae HRPD network also as PLMN identity of the target cell 5.2.2.3.8 eCALL-INACTIVE ------------------------- The UE camps on a suitable cell or an acceptable cell in a PLMN selected as specified in 3GPP S 23.122 [6] but initiates no EMM signalling with the network and ignores any paging requests The UE shall leave substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE state only when one of the following events occur if the USIM is removed, the UE enters substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-IMSI if coverage is lost, the UE enters substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH if the UE is deactivated (e.g. powered off) by the user, the UE enters state EMM-NULL if the UE receives a request from upper layers to establish an eCall over IMS, the UE enters state EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH. The UE then uses the relevant EMM and ESM procedures to establish the eCall over IMS at the earliest opportunity; or if the UE receives a request from upper layers to establish a call to an HPLMN designated non-emergency MSISDN or URI for test or terminal reconfiguration service, the UE enters state EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH. Once the attach procedure is completed, the UE uses the relevant EMM and ESM procedures to establish the non-emergency call

retrieved_contexts.text:
When returning to state EMM-DEREGISTERED, the UE shall select a cell as specified in 3GPP S 36.304 [21]
The substate depends on the result of the cell selection procedure, the outcome of the previously performed EMM specific procedures, on the EPS update status of the UE, on the tracking area data stored in the UE, on the presence of the USIM, on the UE configuration and on the reason for moving to EMM-DEREGISTERED
- If no cell has been found, the substate is NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, until a cell is found
- If no USIM is present or if the inserted USIM is considered invalid by the UE, the substate shall be NO-IMSI
- If a suitable cell has been found and the PLMN or tracking area is not in the forbidden list, the substate shall be NORMAL-SERVICE
- If an attach shall be performed (e.g. network requested re-attach), the substate shall be ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH
- If a PLMN reselection (according to 3GPP S 23.122 [6]) is needed, the substate shall be PLMN-SEARCH
- If the selected cell is known not to be able to provide normal service, the substate shall be LIMITED-SERVICE
- If the selected cell is a non-3GPP cell, the substate shall be NO-CELL-AVAILABLE; and
- If the UE is configured for eCall only mode as specified in 3GPP S 31.102 [17], T3444 and T3445 have expired or are not running, and substate PLMN-SEARCH is not required, the substate shall be eCALL-INACTIVE

results.justification: The model correctly identifies PLMN-SEARCH as the initial substate after power on, which matches the reference. However, the condition for transitioning to EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE is incomplete and partially incorrect. The reference specifies three conditions: timers T3444 and T3445 expired or not running, a PLMN has been selected, AND the UE does not need to perform an eCall over IMS or a call to a non-emergency MSISDN/URI. The model only mentions the eCall-only configuration and the timer condition vaguely, missing the PLMN selection condition and the condition about not needing to perform an eCall over IMS or non-emergency call. The direction is right but key conditions are missing.

results.question: What action should the UE take upon the third expiry of timer T3493 during the Remote UE Report procedure, and what message does it send to report error conditions related to EPS bearer contexts?
results.reference: On the third expiry of timer T3493, the UE shall abort the Remote UE Report procedure and release any resources for this procedure. To report error conditions related to EPS bearer contexts, the UE or network sends an ESM STATUS message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.5, Abnormal cases in the UE; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.15, ESM status
results.model_answer:
On the third expiry of timer T3493, the UE shall **abort the Remote UE Report procedure and release any resources allocated for this procedure**. It does not resend the REMOTE UE REPORT message at this point (that only happens on the first and second expiries).

Regarding error conditions related to EPS bearer contexts: the context provided does not specify any such message (e.g., ESM STATUS) being sent as part of the Remote UE Report procedure's abnormal case handling. The T3493 expiry procedure only addresses retransmission of REMOTE UE REPORT and eventual abortion — no bearer-context-error-reporting message is defined in this clause.

Abnormal cases in the UE
Entities:
- Timer T3493 (Timer): Timer used in the Remote UE Report procedure. On expiry, triggers retransmission of REMOTE UE REPORT message or procedure abortion after third expiry.
- REMOTE UE REPORT (Message): Message sent by UE in Remote UE Report procedure. Retransmitted on first and second T3493 expiry.
- Remote UE Report procedure (Procedure): Procedure for reporting remote UE information. Can be aborted on third T3493 expiry and restarted by UE implementation.
- First expiry of T3493 (Condition): Condition when timer T3493 expires for the first time. UE resends REMOTE UE REPORT and resets/restarts T3493.
- Third expiry of T3493 (Condition): Condition when timer T3493 expires for the third time. UE aborts Remote UE Report procedure and releases resources.
- Release procedure resources (Property): Behavior where UE releases any resources allocated for the Remote UE Report procedure after abortion.
Relations:
- First expiry of T3493 --action_triggered_by--> REMOTE UE REPORT: First expiry of T3493 triggers resending of REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- First expiry of T3493 --resets--> Timer T3493: First expiry of T3493 causes UE to reset and restart timer T3493.
- Third expiry of T3493 --action_triggered_by--> Remote UE Report procedure: Third expiry of T3493 triggers abortion of Remote UE Report procedure.
- Third expiry of T3493 --establishes--> Release procedure resources: Third expiry of T3493 establishes release of procedure resources.
- Remote UE Report procedure --has_step--> REMOTE UE REPORT: Remote UE Report procedure includes sending REMOTE UE REPORT message.

retrieved_contexts.text:
Remote UE Report initiated by the UE
Entities:
- Remote UE Report procedure (Procedure): Procedure initiated by the UE to report information about newly connected or disconnected remote UEs to the network.
- REMOTE UE REPORT (Message): Message sent by the UE to the network to initiate the Remote UE Report procedure.
- REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE (Message): Message sent by the network to the UE in response to the REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- Remote UE information (Information Element): Information about newly connected or disconnected remote UEs included in the REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- Encrypted IMSI remote UE identity (Information Element): Encrypted IMSI identity of a remote UE included in the REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- ProSe Key Management Function address (Information Element): Address of the ProSe Key Management Function corresponding to an encrypted IMSI remote UE identity.
- Default EPS bearer identity (Information Element): Identity of the default EPS bearer associated with the PDN connection for the remote UE.
- T3493 (Timer): Timer started by the UE when sending the REMOTE UE REPORT message and stopped upon receipt of the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message.
- PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING (State): State entered by the UE after sending the REMOTE UE REPORT message and starting timer T3493.
- PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE (State): State entered by the UE after receiving the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message and stopping timer T3493.
- Encrypted IMSI present (Condition): Condition that if any encrypted IMSI remote UE identity is included in the REMOTE UE REPORT message, the UE shall include the corresponding ProSe Key Management Function address.
Relations:
- Remote UE Report procedure --has_step--> REMOTE UE REPORT: The Remote UE Report procedure is initiated by sending the REMOTE UE REPORT message.
- REMOTE UE REPORT --contains_IE--> Remote UE information: The REMOTE UE REPORT message contains information about newly connected or disconnected remote UEs.
- REMOTE UE REPORT --contains_IE--> Default EPS bearer identity: The REMOTE UE REPORT message contains the default EPS bearer identity of the PDN connection associated with the remote UE.
- REMOTE UE REPORT --contains_IE--> Encrypted IMSI remote UE identity: The REMOTE UE REPORT message may contain encrypted IMSI remote UE identities.
- Encrypted IMSI present --guards_by--> ProSe Key Management Function address: If encrypted IMSI is present, the UE shall include the corresponding ProSe Key Management Function address.
- REMOTE UE REPORT --starts--> T3493: Sending the REMOTE UE REPORT message starts timer T3493.
- REMOTE UE REPORT --requires_state--> PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING: After sending the REMOTE UE REPORT message, the UE enters the PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING state.
- REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE --stops--> T3493: Receiving the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message stops timer T3493.
- REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE --requires_state--> PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE: After receiving the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message, the UE enters the PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE state.

retrieved_contexts.text:
The following abnormal cases can be identified
a) Expiry of timer T3493
On the first expiry of the timer T3493, the UE shall resend the REMOTE UE REPORT message and shall reset and restart timer T3493. This retransmission is repeated two times, i.e. on the third expiry of timer T3493, the UE shall abort the procedure and release any resources for this procedure
NOTE: After the abortion of the Remote UE Report procedure, the Remote UE Report procedure for the remote UE(s) can be restarted and how to restart the procedure is left to UE implementation

The UE initiates the Remote UE Report procedure by sending a REMOTE UE REPORT message to the network, starting timer T3493 and entering the state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING (see example in figure 6.6.3.2.1). The UE shall include information of newly connected or disconnected remote UEs to the network in the REMOTE UE REPORT message. If any encrypted IMSI remote UE identity is included in the REMOTE UE REPORT message, the UE shall include the corresponding ProSe Key Management Function address. The UE shall include the default EPS bearer identity of the PDN connection associated with the remote UE connected to the ProSe UE-to-network relay or disconnected from the ProSe UE-to-network relay
NOTE: Encrypted IMSI remote UE identities corresponding to different ProSe Key Management Function addresses need to be reported using separate REMOTE UE REPORT messages
Figure 6.6.3.2.1: Remote UE Report procedure

results.justification: The model correctly identifies that on the third expiry of T3493 the UE aborts the Remote UE Report procedure and releases resources, which matches the reference. However, for the second part of the question about the ESM STATUS message for reporting error conditions related to EPS bearer contexts, the model explicitly denies knowledge of such a message and states none is defined, which contradicts the reference answer. This makes the answer partially correct — right on the abort action, wrong/missing on the ESM STATUS message.

results.question: What are the two network-initiated procedures that change the state of an EPS bearer context, aside from activation?
results.reference: The network has initiated an EPS bearer context modification towards the UE, and the network has initiated an EPS bearer context deactivation towards the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.3.5, BEARER CONTEXT MODIFY PENDING; TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.3.4, BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVE PENDING
results.model_answer:
Aside from activation, the two network-initiated procedures that change the state of an EPS bearer context are:

1. **EPS bearer context modification** procedure
2. **EPS bearer context deactivation** procedure

Entities:

- UE requested bearer resource modification procedure (Procedure): Procedure through which UE can request dedicated bearer activation.
- Attach procedure (Procedure): Procedure during which dedicated bearer activation can occur.

- Service request procedure (Procedure): Procedure whose completion can trigger dedicated bearer activation.
- EMM-IDLE mode (State): EPS Mobility Management idle state.

- BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVE (State): ESM state for inactive EPS bearer contexts.

- TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message (Message): Message that includes EPS bearer context status IE during inter-system mobility.
- Inter-system mobility from WB-S1 to NB-S1 in EMM-IDLE (Condition): Condition triggering local deactivation of dedicated EPS bearer contexts.

- Inter-system mobility from WB-S1 to NB-S1 in EMM-IDLE --establishes--> Local deactivation of dedicated EPS bearer contexts: Inter-system mobility condition triggers local deactivation of dedicated bearers.

- TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message --contains_IE--> EPS bearer context status IE: TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message includes EPS bearer context status IE.
- Local deactivation of dedicated EPS bearer contexts --establishes--> BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVE: Local deactivation sets bearer contexts to INACTIVE state.

retrieved_contexts.text:
Dedicated EPS bearer context activation initiated by the network
Entities:

retrieved_contexts.text:
The purpose of the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure is to establish an EPS bearer context with specific QoS and TFT between the UE and the EPC
In WB-S1 mode, the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure is initiated by the network, but may be requested by the UE by means of the UE requested bearer resource allocation procedure (see clause 6.5.3) or the UE requested bearer resource modification procedure (see clause 6.5.4). The dedicated bearer context activation procedure can be part of the attach procedure or be initiated together with the default EPS bearer context activation procedure when the UE initiated stand-alone PDN connectivity procedure. If the attach procedure or the default EPS bearer context activation procedure fails, the UE shall consider that the dedicated bearer activation has implicitly failed. The network may initiate the dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure together with the completion of the service request procedure
In NB-S1 mode, the dedicated EPS bearer contexts activation procedure is not used
Upon an inter-system mobility from WB-S1 mode to NB-S1 mode in EMM-IDLE mode, if the UE has at least one dedicated EPS bearer context in ESM state BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE, the UE shall locally deactivate any such dedicated EPS bearer context and shall include the EPS bearer context status IE in TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message
Upon an inter-system change from WB-N1 mode to NB-S1 mode in EMM-IDLE mode for the UE operating in single-registration mode, the UE shall set each mapped dedicated EPS bearer context, if any, to ESM state BEARER CONTEXT INACTIVE and shall then include the EPS bearer context status IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message
NOTE: 3GPP S 23.060 [74] clause 9.3 specifies that a packet filter applicable for the downlink direction is not mandatory in a TFT

Two types of ESM procedures can be distinguished
1) Procedures related to EPS bearer contexts
These procedures are initiated by the network and are used for the manipulation of EPS bearer contexts
- default EPS bearer context activation
- dedicated EPS bearer context activation
- EPS bearer context modification
- EPS bearer context deactivation
This procedure is initiated by the network or by the UE and is used for the transport of user data via the control plane
- transport of user data via the control plane procedure
2) Transaction related procedures
These procedures are initiated by the UE to request for resources, i.e. a new PDN connection or dedicated bearer resources, or to release these resources
- PDN connectivity procedure
- PDN disconnect procedure
- bearer resource allocation procedure
- bearer resource modification procedure
This procedure is initiated by the ProSe UE-to-network relay and is used for the manipulation of EPS bearer contexts
- remote UE report
When combined with the attach procedure, the PDN connectivity procedure can trigger the network to execute the following transaction related procedure
- ESM information request procedure
When combined with the attach procedure, if EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is supported by the UE and the network and no PDN connectivity procedure is initiated during the attach procedure, the UE or the network executes the following transaction related procedure
- ESM dummy message procedure
A successful transaction related procedure initiated by the UE triggers the network to execute one of the procedures related to EPS bearer contexts. The UE treats the start of the procedure related to the EPS bearer context as completion of the transaction related procedure
During procedures related to EPS bearer contexts, the MME and the UE shall not initiate the transport of user data via the control plane procedure until the ongoing procedure is completed
NOTE 1: The UE determination of the completion of the transport of user data via the control plane procedure is left to the implementation
NOTE 2: NAS signalling prioritization with respect to the transport of user data via the control plane cannot be guaranteed in the downlink direction in this version of the specification
Except for the remote UE report procedure and ESM information request procedure, during transaction related procedures, the MME and the UE shall not initiate the transport of user data via the control plane procedure until the ongoing procedure is completed
The following ESM procedures can be related to an EPS bearer context or to a procedure transaction
- ESM status procedure

results.justification: The model answer correctly identifies both network-initiated procedures: EPS bearer context modification and EPS bearer context deactivation, which matches the reference answer exactly with no contradictions.

results.question: What are the two specific scenarios in which a UE may include a Release assistance indication IE in an ESM DATA TRANSPORT message, and what is the purpose of this IE?
results.reference: The UE may include a Release assistance indication IE to inform the network that: 1) subsequent to the current uplink data transmission no further uplink or downlink data transmission is expected, or 2) subsequent to the current uplink data transmission only a single downlink data transmission and no further uplink data transmission is expected. The purpose of the IE is to inform the network about the expected pattern of subsequent data transmissions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.4.2, UE initiated transport of user data via the control plane; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.25.2, Release assistance indication
results.model_answer:
The UE may include the Release assistance indication IE in an ESM DATA TRANSPORT message in two scenarios (based on information from upper layers):

1. **No further uplink or downlink data expected** – subsequent to the current uplink data transmission, no further uplink or downlink data transmission (e.g., an acknowledgement or response) is expected; i.e., upper layers indicated that data exchanges have completed with the current UL data transfer.

2. **Only single downlink data expected** – subsequent to the current uplink data transmission, only a single downlink data transmission and no further uplink transmission is expected; i.e., upper layers indicated that data exchanges will be complete once the next downlink data transmission occurs.

**Purpose:** This IE informs the network (MME) about the UE's expected data transmission pattern so that the ESM layer can trigger the EMM layer to initiate release of the NAS signalling connection — either immediately (scenario 1) or after delivery of the next downlink data (scenario 2) — thereby optimizing signalling connection usage for control-plane CIoT data transfers.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.25.1, Message definition

Message definition
Entities:
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT (Message): Message sent by the UE or the network to carry user data in an encapsulated format.
- Protocol discriminator (Information Element): Identifies the protocol type for the message.
- EPS bearer identity (Information Element): Identifies the EPS bearer associated with the data transport.
- Procedure transaction identity (Information Element): Identifies the procedure transaction for the ESM message.
- ESM data transport message identity (Information Element): Identifies the message type as ESM DATA TRANSPORT.
- User data container (Information Element): Carries the encapsulated user data in the message.
- Release assistance indication (Information Element): Optional information element indicating release assistance for the data transfer.
- Release assistance indication optional (Condition): Condition where the release assistance indication IE is optionally present in the message.
Relations:
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT --contains_IE--> Protocol discriminator: ESM DATA TRANSPORT message contains the protocol discriminator IE.
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT --contains_IE--> EPS bearer identity: ESM DATA TRANSPORT message contains the EPS bearer identity IE.
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT --contains_IE--> Procedure transaction identity: ESM DATA TRANSPORT message contains the procedure transaction identity IE.
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT --contains_IE--> ESM data transport message identity: ESM DATA TRANSPORT message contains the ESM data transport message identity IE.
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT --contains_IE--> User data container: ESM DATA TRANSPORT message contains the user data container IE.
- ESM DATA TRANSPORT --contains_IE--> Release assistance indication: ESM DATA TRANSPORT message optionally contains the release assistance indication IE.
- Release assistance indication --guards_by--> Release assistance indication optional: Presence of release assistance indication IE is guarded by optional condition.
